exposure: cardiovascular disease during pregnancy (diagnosed before, during, or up to 6 months after childbirth)
timing of cardiovascular disease diagnosis in relation to pregnancy
outcome: maternal outcomes (e.g., eclampsia, admission to psychiatric ward, one-year mortality)
perinatal outcomes (e.g., preterm birth, small for gestational age)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1,186,137 women aged 15-49 years who were registered in the Swedish Medical Birth Register between 2000 and 2019, accounting for 2,069,107 births.
finding: The prevalence of cardiovascular disease among pregnant women in Sweden increased significantly from 2000-2019, primarily due to arrhythmias, and primiparous women with cardiovascular disease, especially with specific timings of diagnosis, faced a higher risk of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes.
